# The project at a glance

**Question.**

Big question: Can we use dimethyl sulfate (DMS) structure probing techniques to accurately determine pair bases in *in vitro* transcribed human telomerasa RNA (hTR)?

**Data.**

Collected from hTR modified through DMS probing. DMS modification induces base mismatch modification during reverse-transcription which is mapped by Illumina short read sequencing.

| File in `data/raw/`         | Source (link)     | Format | License / terms |
|-----------------------------|-------------------|--------|-----------------|
| `data/raw/266_seq_data.csv` | Experimental data | CSV    | <license>       |

**Folders.**

```         
266A_FINAL
├── run-analysis.qmd   <- render this to run everything
├── README.md          <- points here
├── data/raw          <- never edited
├── data/processed   <- written by the pipeline
├── scripts/               <- one script per step
└── output/            <- figures and tables
```

# Step 1: Import and clean

Data cleaning steps:

```{r}
library("tidyverse")
library("readr")

seq_data <- read.csv("data/raw/266_seq_data.csv")

str(seq_data)

summary(seq_data$mutation[seq_data$sample %in% "hTR_DMS_1" & seq_data$probe %in% "DMS_plus"])
summary(seq_data$mutation[seq_data$sample %in% "hTR_DMS_2" & seq_data$probe %in% "DMS_plus"])
summary(seq_data$mutation[seq_data$sample %in% "hTR_DMS_1" & seq_data$probe %in% "DMS_minus"])
summary(seq_data$mutation[seq_data$sample %in% "hTR_DMS_2" & seq_data$probe %in% "DMS_minus"])

zeros_vals <- seq_data[which(seq_data$raw_read_depth <= 0 | seq_data$effective_depth <= 0), ]   #mutation rate is mutations/read depth so read depths cannot be zero

seq_data$raw_read_depth[seq_data$raw_read_depth <= 0] <- NA    #remove zero values
seq_data$effective_depth[seq_data$effective_depth <= 0] <- NA   #remove zero values
seq_data$raw_read_depth <- as.numeric(seq_data$raw_read_depth)
NA_val <- sum(is.na(seq_data$raw_read_depth), is.na(seq_data$effective_depth))  #check how many NAs are found



if (any(seq_data$raw_read_depth <= 0 | seq_data$effective_depth <= 0, na.rm = TRUE)) stop("zero values must be removed")

str(seq_data)

message("seq_data is cleaned")

write.csv(seq_data, "data/processed/seq_clean.csv", row.names = FALSE)
seq_clean <- read.csv("data/processed/seq_clean.csv")
dim(seq_clean)

```

# Step 2: Process data

```{r}
source("scripts/clean_seq_data.R")

#create two new columns with mutation rates

seq_clean$raw_mut_rate <- seq_clean$mutations / seq_clean$raw_read_depth
seq_clean$effective_mut_rate <- seq_clean$mutations / seq_clean$effective_depth

```

# Step 3: Visualize data

```{r}
source("scripts/clean_seq_data.R")
source("scripts/mut_rate.R")
library(ggplot2)

#| label: hist-raw
raw_mut <- ggplot(seq_clean, aes(x = raw_mut_rate, fill = sample)) + geom_histogram(bins = 120, position = "identity", alpha = 0.5) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 0.1)) + labs(x = "Raw mutation rate", y = "Nucleotide", title = "Raw Mutation Rates")

raw_mut

#| label: hist-eff
eff_mut <- ggplot(seq_clean, aes(x = effective_mut_rate, fill = sample)) + geom_histogram(bins = 200, position = "identity", alpha = 0.5) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 0.1)) + labs(x = "Effective mutation rate", y = "Nucleotide", title = "Effective Mutation Rates")
eff_mut
```

@hist-raw

This plot plot shows distribution of the mutation rate calculated from the raw read depth data which is why I chose to plot this as a histogram.

@hist-eff

Similarly, I plotted the rates calculated with the effective read depth, which is found by more stringent read filtering, as a histogram to represent the distribution for each nucleotide position.

Linear regression correlations:

```{r}

source("scripts/clean_seq_data.R")
source("scripts/mut_rate.R")
library(ggplot2)

seq_clean$raw_DMS1_plus <- seq_clean$raw_mut_rate[seq_clean$sample %in% "hTR_DMS_1" & seq_clean$probe %in% "DMS_plus"]
seq_clean$raw_DMS2_plus <- seq_clean$raw_mut_rate[seq_clean$sample %in% "hTR_DMS_2" & seq_clean$probe %in% "DMS_plus"]
seq_clean$eff_DMS1_plus <- seq_clean$effective_mut_rate[seq_clean$sample %in% "hTR_DMS_1" & seq_clean$probe %in% "DMS_plus"]
seq_clean$eff_DMS2_plus <- seq_clean$effective_mut_rate[seq_clean$sample %in% "hTR_DMS_2" & seq_clean$probe %in% "DMS_plus"]

#| label: corr-raw
raw_corr_plus_plot <- ggplot(seq_clean, aes(x = raw_DMS1_plus, y = raw_DMS2_plus)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) + labs(x = "Raw DMS 1 mutation rate", y = "Raw DMS 1 mutation rate", title = "Raw DMS correlation")

raw_corr_plus_plot

raw_plus_corr <- lm(raw_DMS1_plus ~ raw_DMS2_plus, data = seq_clean)
coef(raw_plus_corr)
summary(raw_plus_corr)

#| label: corr-eff
eff_corr_plus_plot <- ggplot(seq_clean, aes(x = eff_DMS1_plus, y = eff_DMS2_plus)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) + labs(x = "Effective DMS 1 mutation rate", y = "Effective DMS 1 mutation rate", title = "Effective DMS correlation")

eff_corr_plus_plot

eff_plus_corr <- lm(eff_DMS1_plus ~ eff_DMS2_plus, data = seq_clean)
coef(eff_plus_corr)
summary(eff_plus_corr)
nobs(eff_plus_corr)

raw_diag_df <- data.frame(raw_fitted = fitted(raw_plus_corr), raw_resid  = residuals(raw_plus_corr))

raw_residual <- ggplot(raw_diag_df, aes(x = raw_fitted, y = raw_resid)) + geom_point() + geom_hline(yintercept = 0) + labs(x = "Fitted raw mutation rate", y = "Residual", title = "Raw read residuals")

raw_residual

eff_diag_df <- data.frame(eff_fitted = fitted(eff_plus_corr), eff_resid  = residuals(eff_plus_corr))

eff_residual <- ggplot(eff_diag_df, aes(x = eff_fitted, y = eff_resid)) + geom_point() + geom_hline(yintercept = 0) + labs(x = "Fitted effective mutation rate", y = "Residual", title = "Effective read residuals")

eff_residual
```

The correlation between replicates shown by the coefficient values was low for the raw DMS samples but higher for the effective DMS samples. Meaning the more stringent read filtering helped reduce the noise. I check this with residual plots which both showed points collecting mostly around 0.
